title: ARCH↔FE-001: Data/Event Contracts for Visualization + UX-Driven Data Needs
description: The Embedded Systems Architect provides data/event contracts for visualization (telemetry and event payload schemas with field definitions and units), real-time stream topology (MQTT-over-WebSockets topic structures, message schemas, QoS), and the semantics of inference outputs to be displayed (confidence scores, drift signals, model-version metadata); the Frontend/Dashboard Engineer provides UX-driven data needs (payload shape, update frequency, aggregation requirements), monitoring/alerting visualization requirements, and feedback on contract gaps raised via the ADR process with evidence. Grounded in EMBEDDED_SYSTEMS_ARCHITECT_SKILL §6.9 and FRONTEND_DASHBOARD_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.9.

visualization_contracts.description: ARCH→FE: data/event contracts, stream topology, inference-output semantics.

unit.description: Explicit unit for every physical quantity (units rule §3.10); use 'enum'/'bool'/'string'/'timestamp' for non-physical fields.

inference_output_semantics.description: Semantics of model outputs to display.

ux_data_needs.description: FE→ARCH: UX-driven data needs and contract-gap feedback.

contract_gaps.description: Contract gaps are raised via the ADR process with evidence.

adr_ref.description: Gap raised via an ADR with evidence.

x-macp.tier_rationale: Routine data/event-contract definition for dashboard visualization is agent-autonomous. Contract gaps are raised via the ADR process (with evidence), and any breaking change to a ratified visualization data contract requires a CCR + version bump.
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER (contract definition at planning; integration checkpoints during development; alert-semantics review before production)
confirm_conditions: data_event_contracts are present and every field carries an explicit unit (or a non-physical type marker)
stream topology and QoS are specified where a real-time stream is provided
inference-output semantics are defined for any model output to be displayed (confidence, drift, model version)
FE UX-driven update frequencies carry an explicit unit
reject_conditions: a telemetry/event field emitted without a unit (units rule §3.10)
a contract gap asserted without an adr_ref + evidence (gaps must be raised via the ADR process)
a breaking change to a ratified visualization contract made without a CCR + version bump
counter_conditions: a requested update frequency exceeds the contracted stream cadence — request a feasible rate or a server-side aggregation
alerting threshold semantics are ambiguous — request the Architect's system-event taxonomy mapping before wiring alerts
